title: Cross-Program Accounts: Insulin Pharmacy Balances and Insulin Pump Program Payment Plans
content:
**Which insulin pharmacy balance lengthens a pump payment plan?**
The insulin-balance extension of a payment plan on an Insulin Pump Program follows the balance of the customer's active Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program whose delivery method is insulin pump:

| Balance of that active insulin pharmacy program | Effect on the plan months |
|---|---|
| at least the pump tier's payment-plan minimum balance | 2 months (the long insulin-balance extension) are added |
| above zero and below that minimum | 1 month (the short insulin-balance extension) is added |
| zero or less, or no such active program | nothing is added |

**Which minimum balance applies?**
That of the pump program's tier: $150.00 on the Insulin Pump Self-Pay Program, the Insulin Pump Commercial HMO Program and the Insulin Pump Commercial PPO Program; $100.00 on the Insulin Pump Medicare Advantage Program, the Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program and the Insulin Pump Medicaid Program.

**Does an insulin pharmacy program that delivers by pen count?**
No — only the active insulin pharmacy program whose delivery method is insulin pump is read.

**Examples (hypothetical, pump program on the Medicare Advantage tier):** a pump-delivery insulin program balance of $100.00 adds 2 months; $40.00 adds 1 month; $0.00 adds nothing.
